root: Let's build a verb from scratch. Every verb starts as a root from the list of roots, the Dhātupāṭha. Our root is भू, to be. Tap it to see its entry.
tense: First, tense. We want the present: is, right now. Pāṇini marks tense with abstract placeholders called lakāras. Pick the right one.
ending: The ल् is only a placeholder. It must be replaced by a real personal ending. We want third person singular: he or she is. Pick the ending from the table.
vikarana: Verbs of the first class need a connector between root and ending. Sūtra 3.1.68 brings in शप्, which, once its tags fall away, is just अ.
guna: Before an affix like this अ, the root vowel strengthens to its guṇa, by sūtra 7.3.84. ऊ is a lip vowel. Which guṇa is nearest?
sandhi: Last step. ओ now meets अ. By sūtra 6.1.78, ओ becomes अव् before a vowel. What is the finished word?
review: Here is the whole derivation as vidyut computes it, all twenty steps, with the big moves highlighted. Then a short quiz.
